{{Short description|Infinite game in descriptive set theory whose payoff set is a lightface analytic set}}
{{more citations needed|date=October 2014}}
{{LLM|date=April 2026}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=October 2023}}
In [[descriptive set theory]], a '''lightface analytic game''' is an infinite two-player game of perfect information whose payoff set is a [[lightface]] [[Analytic set|analytic]] ('''Σ{{sup|1}}{{sub|1}}''') subset of [[Baire space]]. The determinacy of all lightface analytic games is equivalent, over [[ZFC]], to the existence of [[Zero sharp|0{{sup|#}}]], a result known as the '''Martin–Harrington theorem'''.

== Background ==

=== Infinite games ===
The games studied here are [[Gale-Stewart game]]s. Two players, conventionally called Player I and Player II, alternate choosing natural numbers, with Player I going first:

: Player I chooses ''a''{{sub|0}}, Player II chooses ''a''{{sub|1}}, Player I chooses ''a''{{sub|2}}, ...

After infinitely many rounds, the two players have together produced an infinite sequence (''a''{{sub|0}}, ''a''{{sub|1}}, ''a''{{sub|2}}, ...) in [[Baire space (set theory)|Baire space]] ''ω''{{sup|''ω''}} — the set of all infinite sequences of natural numbers equipped with the product of the discrete topology. A payoff set ''A'' ⊆ ''ω''{{sup|''ω''}} is fixed in advance; Player I wins if the resulting sequence belongs to ''A'', and Player II wins otherwise.

A '''strategy''' for Player I is a function σ that maps each finite sequence of even length (representing the moves played so far) to a natural number (Player I's next move). A strategy for Player II is defined analogously for sequences of odd length. A strategy is a '''winning strategy''' if following it guarantees a win regardless of the opponent's play. A game is '''[[Determined game|determined]]''' if one of the two players has a winning strategy.

=== The determinacy hierarchy ===
Not all infinite games are determined: using the [[axiom of choice]] one can construct an undetermined game.<ref>{{cite book |last=Jech |first=Thomas |title=Set Theory |publisher=Springer |year=2003 |isbn=3-540-44085-2 |edition=3rd millennium}}</ref> However, determinacy holds for payoff sets of low descriptive complexity. The classical results form a hierarchy:

== Lightface versus boldface ==
The [[Analytical hierarchy#Lightface and boldface hierarchies|lightface/boldface distinction]] is central to this subject. A set ''A'' ⊆ ''ω''{{sup|''ω''}} is '''boldface''' analytic ('''Σ{{sup|1}}{{sub|1}}''') if it is the projection of a closed set in a product space, equivalently if there exists a tree ''T'' on ''ω'' × ''ω'' such that ''A'' is the set of first coordinates of infinite branches through ''T''. The '''lightface''' version adds an effectivity constraint: ''A'' is lightface analytic ('''Σ{{sup|1}}{{sub|1}}''') if ''T'' can be taken to be a [[Computable set|computable]] (recursive) subset of (''ω'' × ''ω''){{sup|<''ω''}}.<ref>{{cite book |last=Moschovakis |first=Yiannis N. |title=Descriptive Set Theory |publisher=American Mathematical Society |year=2009 |isbn=978-0-8218-4813-5 |edition=2nd}}</ref>

Equivalently, a set is lightface analytic if it is [[recursively enumerable]] relative to no oracle — it can be described without any real-number parameters. Boldface analytic sets may require real-number parameters; the lightface class is strictly smaller.

This distinction has a direct consequence for determinacy: boldface analytic determinacy follows from the existence of a [[measurable cardinal]], a relatively strong large-cardinal assumption. Lightface analytic determinacy requires only the weaker assumption that [[Zero sharp|0{{sup|#}}]] exists. Conversely, [[Leo Harrington]] showed that lightface analytic determinacy cannot be proved in ZFC alone, and in fact implies the existence of 0{{sup|#}}.

== The Martin–Harrington theorem ==
The central result of the subject is:
{{blockquote|'''Theorem''' (Martin–Harrington, 1978). The following are equivalent over ZFC:
# All lightface analytic games are determined.
# [[Zero sharp|0{{sup|#}}]] exists.}}

=== Forward direction: 0{{sup|#}} implies determinacy ===
[[Donald A. Martin]] proved that if 0{{sup|#}} exists then all lightface analytic games are determined.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Martin |first=Donald A. |year=1970 |title=Measurable cardinals and analytic games |journal=[[Fundamenta Mathematicae]] |volume=66 |pages=287–291 |doi=10.4064/fm-66-3-287-291}}</ref> The key tool is the sequence of [[Silver indiscernibles]] encoded by 0{{sup|#}}. These indiscernibles provide a uniform way to build winning strategies for lightface analytic games: the computable tree defining the payoff set can be analyzed using the indiscernibles, and the resulting structure allows one to determine which player wins and to explicitly construct a winning strategy.

=== Reverse direction: determinacy implies 0{{sup|#}} ===
[[Leo Harrington]] proved the converse in 1978: if all lightface analytic games are determined, then 0{{sup|#}} exists.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Harrington |first=Leo A. |year=1978 |title=Analytic determinacy and 0{{sup|#}} |journal=[[Journal of Symbolic Logic]] |volume=43 |issue=4 |pages=685–693 |doi=10.2307/2273508 |jstor=2273508}}</ref> This direction is considerably harder. Harrington's proof uses the theory of [[Admissible set|admissible sets]] and [[Admissible ordinal|admissible ordinals]] (in particular, [[Barwise compactness]]) to show that determinacy of a certain lightface analytic game forces the existence of a model of set theory with a non-trivial [[elementary embedding]] ''j'' : ''L'' → ''L'', which is equivalent to the existence of 0{{sup|#}}. A later forcing-free proof of this direction was given by Sami (1999).<ref>{{cite journal |last=Sami |first=Ramez L. |year=1999 |title=Analytic determinacy and 0{{sup|#}}: a forcing-free proof of Harrington's theorem |journal=[[Fundamenta Mathematicae]] |volume=160 |issue=2 |pages=153–159 |doi=10.4064/fm-160-2-153-159}}</ref>

== 0{{sup|#}} and the constructible universe ==
[[Zero sharp|0{{sup|#}}]] (zero sharp) is a real number — formally a subset of ''ω'' — that encodes the complete first-order theory of [[Constructible universe|Gödel's constructible universe ''L'']] with respect to its [[Silver indiscernibles]]. The Silver indiscernibles are a [[Club set|club]] class of ordinals that are indistinguishable from one another by any first-order formula of set theory with parameters from lower in the indiscernible sequence.

The existence of 0{{sup|#}} is independent of ZFC. If 0{{sup|#}} exists then ''L'' ≠ ''V'' (the constructible universe is a proper inner model of the true universe), and every uncountable cardinal of ''V'' is a [[measurable cardinal]] in ''L''[0{{sup|#}}]. The existence of a measurable cardinal implies that 0{{sup|#}} exists, but not conversely; 0{{sup|#}} is a strictly weaker assumption.

== Relativization ==
The theorem relativizes to arbitrary reals. For any real ''x'', '''Π{{sup|1}}{{sub|1}}(''x'')''' determinacy — determinacy of all games whose payoff set is lightface co-analytic relative to ''x'' as an oracle — is equivalent to the existence of '''x{{sup|#}}''', the sharp for the inner model ''L''[''x''].<ref>{{cite book |last=Kanamori |first=Akihiro |title=The Higher Infinite |publisher=Springer |year=2003 |isbn=3-540-00384-3 |edition=2nd}}</ref> The original Martin–Harrington theorem is the special case ''x'' = ∅.
